title: Import organizations, sites, contacts or external identifiers
purpose: Upload one CSV file of organizations, sites, contacts or external identifiers, check the preview of what each row would do, and import every row or none.
summary: Upload a CSV file, read the preview of each row's action and problems, then import the whole file. Nothing is saved before you import.

tasks.title: Check and import a file
steps: Choose the file under [[CSV file (UTF-8)]] and select [[Check file]].
Read the preview: errors are listed first, then rows with formula-like cells.
If the file changes existing records, give the [[Reason for changing existing records]].
Select the Import button. It names the number of rows.

tasks.title: Fix a file with errors
steps: Correct the rows named in Problems in your spreadsheet.
Select [[Upload a corrected file]] and check it again. Nothing was saved.

good_to_know: One error anywhere blocks the whole file; nothing is saved until every row is clean.
If the file, its name, a record it changes or the organization a code points to changed after the preview, the import is refused and a fresh preview is shown.
A cell starting with =, +, - or @ is flagged because spreadsheet programs treat it as a formula. It is imported as text, unchanged.
Every created or changed record keeps the file name and its SHA-256 in its history, and the file adds one summary entry.

items.label: CSV file (UTF-8)
items.description: Required. Comma separated, header row first, up to 1024 KiB and 2000 rows. Save it from your spreadsheet as CSV UTF-8; a byte-order mark is fine, other encodings are refused.

items.label: Check file
items.description: Reads the file and shows the preview. It runs every row through the same checks as the forms, then undoes everything: the preview leaves no record and no history entry.

items.label: Columns
items.description: Lists every column of this file with whether it is required, its format and its meaning. Key columns identify the record: account_code for organizations; account_code and site_code for sites; account_code and email for contacts, or account_code and name for a contact without an email. A column left out of the file leaves that value alone; a blank cell clears an optional value.

items.label: Record
items.description: The record the row names by its keys, such as EXGEN or EXGEN · ED.

items.label: Line
items.description: The line in the file, counting the header as line 1.

items.label: Values (before → after)
items.description: For a new record the values it gets; for a change, each changed value before and after.

items.label: Problems
items.description: What blocks the row, naming the column; cells flagged as formula-like; values marked Not applied because the record they belong to is already recorded and shared; and notes, such as an existing link being attached.

items.label: Reason for changing existing records
items.description: Shown and required when the file changes existing records. It is kept in each changed record's history with the file name and SHA-256.

items.label: Import
items.description: Checks the file and the records it changes again, then saves every row through the same services as the forms, or nothing. Afterwards the client organization list opens with a summary. A file that matches the records already changes nothing.

items.label: Start over
items.description: Returns to an empty upload form.

sections.title: Rules by file
paragraphs: Organizations: a parent_account_code must name an organization that exists or comes in an earlier row; a loop is refused. A new organization with the name of an existing one is refused; use that organization's account code instead. account_owner is the username of an active laboratory staff account.

Sites and contacts are always found inside the organization their row names, so a row never moves a site or contact to another organization. site_codes lists sites of that same organization. A contact known only by name gains the email address the row gives it.

External identifiers: each row links an organization to a record in an external system by the system's key, the record type, an optional identifier scheme and the identifier, in a role (related unless given). An identifier that is already recorded is attached as it is: the import never changes a recorded link's label or address, which other organizations and tickets may share, and lists any difference on the row as Not applied; change it on the link's page instead. Patient, participant and donor identifiers are refused and never shown in the preview: they belong on a ticket, behind the patient-information permission. An address is accepted only when the system has a base address, and must then be https on that host. An import and a change that puts an organization into a group, or another import, take turns: whichever starts second waits for the first to be saved. If the database still has to stop the import because it and another change are waiting for each other, the page says so and nothing is imported; upload it again.
